summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted for sudden-onset epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the substernal area, associated with nausea but no vomiting. Initial evaluation revealed hyperkalemia (K+ 6.7), managed with insulin, calcium gluconate, and hemodialysis, with subsequent normalization of potassium. Cardiac workup including serial troponins and EKG showed no acute ischemia despite baseline elevations due to renal disease. CT abdomen/pelvis showed cholelithiasis without cholecystitis, no appendicitis, and no evidence of mesenteric ischemia. Abdominal pain improved significantly by the second hospital day. A right upper quadrant ultrasound confirmed gallstones without signs of inflammation. A new small lung nodule was noted and recommended for outpatient follow-up. The patient was discharged home with home health services for insulin management after a glucose of 400 prompted initiation of a sliding scale regimen. He was instructed to continue dialysis, monitor weight, adhere to a low-sodium diet, and follow up with primary care and GI.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
